LESSON: SIGN READING 9.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we tell the characters in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. make predictions as they sign about a story based on the title and pictures,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to direct and indirect questions about a text to show comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. visualise characters, events, and places for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. adopt sign reading pictures and texts for information. • In groups, learners are guided to brainstorm as they sign about the title of a story. • Individually, learner is guided to make predictions as they sign of what will happen in a story based on the title and pictures. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify and sign the characters and setting of a story. • Individually, learner is guided to respond to direct and indirect questions from the signed text read. • In groups, learners are guided to develop a concept map from a text related to theme with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to retell a story as they sign in a few words. How do we tell the characters in a story?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 9.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner uses a concept map to show comprehension.

● Creativity and imagination: as the learner predicts events/outcomes of a story: Cooperation is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to

develop a concept map from the text read based on the title and pictures.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to develop a concept map from the text read.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: social cohesion by working with peers in pairs to retell the story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the comprehension strategies when reading texts in Environmental Activities.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. make predictions as they sign about a story based on the title and pictures,
2. respond to direct and indirect questions about a text to show comprehension,
3. visualise characters, events, and places for comprehension,
4. adopt sign reading pictures and texts for information. • In groups, learners are guided to brainstorm as they sign about the title of a story. • Individually, learner is guided to make predictions as they sign of what will happen in a story based on the title and pictures. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify and sign the characters and setting of a story. • Individually, learner is guided to respond to direct and indirect questions from the signed text read. • In groups, learners are guided to develop a concept map from a text related to theme with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to retell a story as they sign in a few words.
